messages:
ajay: noticed regression in tenant fairness after yesterday's kernel tweak — short sessions latencies dropped but several tenants with long contexts spiked in p95.

maria: yep, dashboard flagged hostpool-3 and hostpool-9. KV hit-rate dipped ~7% concurrently.

ajay: digging into scheduler traces: batcher is forming many tiny micro-batches (avg tokens/batch down from 28 -> 6) which fragments slots and increases wait time for long requests.

lina: do we have perf profiles? GPU L2 miss patterns or SM occupancy changes?

ajay: grabbing the quick sample: L2 misses up by ~6% for the new GEMM path on small batch sizes. Also more kernel switches per second which seems to thrash caches.

omar: hypothesis: kernel selector flips opportunistically to fastest int8 path for short sequences, then flips back for next request types causing churn. That plus tiny micro-batches is killing KV locality.

maria: simple mitigation we tried locally: reserve a fraction of each slot for long contexts so they don't starve. That reduced long-tenant tail significantly in canary.

lina: suggestion: implement token-reserve per-slot and a deficit counter. If a tenant received fewer tokens over the last window, bump their allocation priority until they catch up.

omar: agree. Proposal details:
- slot_reserve_ratio = 0.25
- deficit_decay_window_sec = 600
- deficit_prioritization_weight = 2.0
This keeps short request latency reasonable while protecting long sequences.

ajay: also add kernel-selection hysteresis: only allow switching kernels if new kernel is >X% better for Y consecutive requests or after Z ms. Cuts flip-flopping.

maria: KV prefetching: tag prefetches with cohort ids so we avoid evicting cohort A when prioritizing cohort B. Also emit cohort hit/miss metrics.

lina: operational guardrails: add a perf-gate that runs a 3-mix microbench nightly (short-heavy, long-heavy, balanced). Block kernel rollouts if kv_hit_rate drops >5% or p99 latency reg >8%.

ops-bot: created job runtime/mix-smoke-nightly and alert rule runtime.mix_smoke.block_on_regression.

omar: we should also instrument "micro-batch churn" metric (micro_batches_per_second) and add it to the alerting/graphing.

ajay: ran 50k request canary with slot_reserve_ratio=0.3 and deficit scoring. Results:
- long-tenant p95 from 5.6s -> 2.3s
- short-tenant p95 from 0.85s -> 1.05s
- kv_hit_rate recovered by ~6%
Tradeoff but much less starvation.

maria: config snippet we tested:

```
batcher:
  allocator: hybrid
  slot_reserve_ratio: 0.30
  max_micro_batches: 6
  defrag_ms: 40
  deficit_window_sec: 600
kernel_selector:
  min_stable_duration_ms: 400
  min_improvement_pct: 7
kv:
  cohort_prefetch: true
  cohort_ttl_sec: 1200
```

lina: add a cheap fairness dashboard: tokens_allocated_per_tenant (1m rolling) + deficit_score + p95 per-tenant. That will give visibility before things escalate.

omar: one implementation note: keep deficit scoring lock-free and approximate (exponential decay counters) to avoid scheduler contention.

maria: rollout plan: 1) enable metrics + cohort tagging on prod hosts (no behavior change), 2) deploy slot_reserve + deficit on 5% canary for 12h, monitor, 3) widen to 25% for 48h, 4) full rollout if stable.

ajay: add perf-gate for new GEMM paths: require nightly microbench with representative mixes to pass or else auto-block deploys.

ops-bot: created RFC and rollout task in INF-2187 and set canary gates.

lina: I'll prepare the dashboard panels and wire the micro-bench to CI so we get immediate feedback on PRs touching the kernel.

maria: I'll add cohort metrics to KV and correlate eviction rates with deficit priority changes.

ajay: thanks. I'll open a short postmortem on the kernel ramp noting missing perf gate and no fairness sim coverage. Attach canary logs and config.

ops-bot: postmortem ticket INF-2189 created.

maria: tagging @oncall for awareness. :eyes:
